text: Optional smooth exact-off response: aε(q) = 0 for q ≤ 0, and aε(q) = q exp[−(ε/q)²] for q > 0. For fixed ε > 0 this scalar function is C∞, including the join at zero. Using aε(qδ) with fixed δ > 0 makes the constitutive response smooth in the gradient variable and exactly zero when qδ ≤ 0. This is an alternative to the tanh law, not a property of it. Its positive onset in the original magnitude is |∇S| > √(Γcrit² + 2δΓcrit), so the threshold must be calibrated in the chosen measure. To retain the original cutoff |∇S| = Γcrit instead, use the calibrated excess qδ* = √(|∇S|² + δ²) − √(Γcrit² + δ²). It has the same sign as |∇S| − Γcrit for Γcrit ≥ 0. Using aε(qδ*) gives a smooth exact-off alternative with that original cutoff; the response above it is still a changed constitutive law.
